phase_0.boundary_condition: the composite integer N whose non-trivial factor is extracted
phase_0.domain_name: Pollard's rho factor extraction: initialize tortoise and hare walkers
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: iteration of f(x) = x^2 + c mod N advancing a walker
AFWD.justification: each application moves the state forward along the pseudo-random sequence

AREV.chosen_element: retry with new parameters c and x0 after trivial gcd
AREV.justification: a failed cycle descends back to re-initialization with fresh constants

CLINK.chosen_element: chaining tortoise step then hare double-step per loop
CLINK.justification: the two advances compose sequentially to form one Floyd cycle-detection round

ENGAGR.chosen_element: dialetheia x ≡ y (mod p) ∧ x ≢ y (mod N) held during walk
ENGAGR.justification: the congruence modulo the unknown factor p and non-congruence modulo N coexist as the engine of detection

EVALF.chosen_element: gcd(|x-y|, N) = 1 indicating no factor yet
EVALF.justification: constructive refutation that the current cycle yields a divisor

EVALT.chosen_element: non-trivial factor d = gcd(|x-y|, N) with 1 < d < N
EVALT.justification: constructive proof that a proper divisor of N has been found

FFUSE.chosen_element: rejoin after parameter retry or factor acceptance
FFUSE.justification: arms converge: trivial gcd triggers retry, non-trivial factor terminates, failure restarts

FSPLIT.chosen_element: branch on gcd(|x-y|, N) after each hare advance
FSPLIT.justification: splits into trivial factor (1), non-trivial factor (1<d<N), and failure (N)

IFIX.chosen_element: append discovered factor d to the factorization log
IFIX.justification: permanent, append-only record of the extracted divisor for downstream use

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the polynomial f(x) = x^2 + c mod N as a fixed object
IMSCRIB.justification: the function is self-identical across all iterations; it does not transform

TANCH.chosen_element: extracted factor d where 1 < d < N
TANCH.justification: the computation halts with a non-trivial divisor of N in hand

VINIT.justification: no walkers, no function parameters, no modulus bound

phase_2.fuse_element: rejoin after parameter retry or factor acceptance
phase_2.fuse_result: either a verified factor d or a fresh parameter set (c, x0) for restart
phase_2.rejoin_note: trivial gcd continues the walk; non-trivial factor terminates; gcd=N triggers AREV retry with new c, x0 then re-enters the walk loop
phase_2.split_element: branch on gcd(|x-y|, N) after each hare advance
phase_2.split_input: current pair (x, y) and modulus N
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: a live contradiction, the paraconsistent resolution
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither: uninitialized, nothing established

steps.domain_action: request arrives with composite N and no parameters
select seed x0 and constant c, bind f(x) = x^2 + c mod N
fix polynomial f as the iteration function
hold dialetheia x ≡ y (mod p) ∧ x ≢ y (mod N) as loop invariant
compose tortoise step and hare double-step into one round
compute g = gcd(|tortoise - hare|, N), g = 1
continue next round with updated walkers
compute g = gcd(|tortoise - hare|, N), 1 < g < N
append factor g to factorization log
compute g = gcd(|tortoise - hare|, N), g = N
discard walkers, select new c and x0
reinitialize tortoise = x0, hare = x0 with new parameters
rejoin into walk loop with fresh constants
record retry event in audit log

phase_5.alfs_store: Pollard's original 1975 paper and standard computational number theory texts
phase_5.compiler_frontend: the number-theoretic specification mapping N to polynomial parameters
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: shared integer registers for tortoise, hare, and gcd values
phase_5.memory_mechanism: modular arithmetic unit holding N, c, x0, and intermediate residues
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Floyd cycle-detection loop driving tortoise/hare advances

phase_6.cycle_cost: O(√p) modular multiplications where p is the smallest prime factor of N
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — each iteration conserves state size; entropy cost is the expected number of steps to collision modulo p
phase_6.post_cycle_state: non-trivial factor d recorded, N reduced to cofactor N/d
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: composite N with unknown factorization, no walkers initialized
